Recent work supports learning recommendation-specific text representations, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of GRU4Rec, a text encoder trained from scratch, and semantic hard-negative mining. [Recformer (KDD 2023)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf) jointly learns language understanding and sequential recommendation, using a Transformer and pretraining. [DWSRec (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) addresses anisotropy in pretrained text embeddings. Both offer motivation for text features, not direct evidence for the permitted architecture or no-pretraining setting.

False negatives are a central concern: semantic similarity can identify useful competitors but also plausible unobserved positives. [UFNRec (SDM 2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) identifies suspected false negatives and applies positive reassignment and teacher-provided soft labels. Its teacher mechanism is unnecessary for the proposed single-model experiment. [A 2024 sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive sampling; results vary with dataset and item popularity, so harder sampling has no universal advantage.

A compatible experimental hypothesis: jointly train randomly initialized token embeddings plus a small pooled-text encoder, integrate title/description features with item-ID embeddings inside one GRU network, and use one scoring function. Compare uniform sampling against a modest mixture of uniform and text-similar candidates; exclude observed training positives and test conservative weighting of ambiguous negatives. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated findings. Text similarity alone cannot establish product compatibility, satisfied needs, or dislike. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category.
